properties.description:
FFWFFC

The National Weather Service in Peachtree City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Dawson County in north central Georgia...
Southeastern Fannin County in north central Georgia...
Southeastern Gilmer County in north central Georgia...
Northeastern Pickens County in north central Georgia...

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Jasper, Talking Rock, Cartecay, Roy, Sequoyah Lake, Lake Tamarack,
Pisgah, Black Gap Shelter, Stover Creek Shelter and Springer
Mountain Shelter.

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 1:02AM MDT until September 23 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east central, north central, northeast,
northwest, and west central New Mexico, including the following
areas, in east central New Mexico, Quay County. In north central
New Mexico, Far Northwest Highlands, Northern Sangre de Cristo
Mountains, Tusas Mountains Including Chama and Upper Rio Grande
Valley. In northeast New Mexico, Johnson and Bartlett Mesas
Including Raton Pass and Union County. In northwest New Mexico,
Chuska Mountains and Northwest Plateau. In west central New Mexico,
San Francisco River Valley and West Central Plateau.

* WHEN...From noon MDT today through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A dangerous surge of monsoon moisture will arrive today and
Wednesday with widespread heavy rain.  Scattered occurrences of
flash flooding are likely, and there will probably be some main
stem river and tributary flooding, as the most likely rain amount
by Wednesday afternoon exceeds 1.5 inches many locations along
and east of the central mountain chain, and 1 inch in many
locations westward to around Dulce, Gallup, and Glenwood.
Stronger storms will produce torrential rainfall at rates over 2
inches per hour, and storms will train repeatedly in succession
over some locations, with locally heavier rain amounts reaching
over 4 inches over portions of southern, central, and eastern New
Mexico.  Heavy rain will likely continue Wednesday night over
north-central and eastern New Mexico, then showers and storms
with locally heavy rainfall are forecast to return to much of the
state again on Thursday.
- Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex
terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas,
normally dry arroyos, and near rivers and streams.  As the event
unfolds, locations with saturated ground will also become prone
to rapid runoff and flash flooding from additional rounds of
storms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 22 at 4:48PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
An active monsoon pattern will continue across western Micronesia
with satellite imagery continuing to show areas of heavy showers and
thunderstorms. Latest satellite-dervied surface wind data depicts 15
to 20 mph west to southwest winds across western Yap State and Palau
with pockets of locally higher winds.

Weather models point to a continuation of these conditions with
periods of locally heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts, and choppy seas. Both
Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of Invest 91W, located near
13N142E, northeast of Yap. 91W is now the subject of a Tropical
Cyclone Formation Alert from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center and
showers are expected to remain mostly numerous to widespread and
heavy at times. Model guidance suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain per day
will be possible through Wednesday, especially for Yap.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next couple of days.
Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 22 at 4:12PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Conditions have generally tapered down across Majuro from yesterdays
wind and rain event. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms
will bring some locally heavy showers through tonight. Further north,
a tropical disturbance has produced robust convection across Bikini
Atoll and the far northern Marshall Islands today. This morning's
scatterometer shows that gusts could be approaching 40 to 45 knots in
the heaviest showers and thunderstorms. Some of this heavy weather
has made it as far south of Kwajalein today. Over the next couple of
days, model guidance shows a westward shift of the tropical
disturbance with a slow weakening trend. Scattered showers will
remain possible across the RMI this week with a monsoon-like pattern
remaining in place.

Seas could approach 9 to 12 feet where the strongest winds and
heaviest showers occur. This would make conditions hazardous to
Small Craft across the far northern RMI with extreme choppiness.
Boaters moving through the Marshall Islands north of Kwajalein
should practice enhanced caution over the next day or so.

For more information keep up to date with the latest information
from the Majuro Weather Service office and your local emergency
management agency.

properties.description:
We are currently tracking a low that is expected to move through
the southern Bering Sea Thursday through Saturday and which could
approach the coast of the YK Delta. While the most likely storm
track south of our area would result in only modest rises in above
normal high water, a further north track could result in high
surf potential. As of right now, the southern portion of the YK
Delta coast could see water levels rise to around 1 to 3 feet
above the mean high water line. We will continue to monitor this
system closely.
